about: Case file CF8's data: the studies' dated steps (LX.Timeline; an E13 event's footer is the approved acknowledgement, drawn under it by the page's script), where the result holds (LX.Boundary) and the toy's settings. Research text here is approved excerpt wording (reports/learn/excerpts_for_approval.md, E12 and E13, approved 2026-11-05); the toy reuses lesson M9's illustrative turbine and records (m09-surrogates-uq.json).

events.label: Related research project, 2022–2023
events.text: A research project asks whether uncertainty metrics of a wind power model's inputs can predict calibrated plant-level power uncertainty at plants without power measurements.
events.footer: This work was developed based upon funding from the Alliance for Sustainable Energy, LLC, Managing and Operating Contractor for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory for the U.S. Department of Energy.

events.label: Conference paper (this case)
events.text: A turbine type's theoretical power curve and measured records, condensed by kernel density sampling, are fused by multi-fidelity Gaussian process regression; presented at ASME IDETC 2023 (20–23 August 2023), online in November 2023.

source.label: Li et al. (2023), ASME IDETC 2023, V03AT03A034

events.label: Code released

events.label: Code released
events.text: A documented, runnable framework for the uncertainty metrics and the surrogate workflow, implemented afresh and tested on synthetic data (version 1.0.0).
events.footer: This work was developed based upon funding from the Alliance for Sustainable Energy, LLC, Managing and Operating Contractor for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory for the U.S. Department of Energy.

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: one wind farm's records from one open dataset;
one generic theoretical curve for the turbine type;
point scores for nine test turbines and probabilistic scores for one;
which model ranks first depends on the metric.
leaves: other wind farms, datasets and theoretical curves.
boundary.source: From the approved excerpt of Li et al. (2023), ASME IDETC 2023.

idea.title: From a band on the curve to a band on the capacity factor (illustrative)
idea.note: Lesson M9's toy turbine and records: invented round numbers, not the study's data.
idea.scope: The band is the fitted curve's uncertainty only: the expected capacity factor, with the wind-speed mix and the fit's settings held fixed. It leaves out year-to-year weather and operating changes.
idea.levelNote: 90% band: if the fitted model is right, the expected capacity factor lies inside it with probability 0.9.
idea.caption: Expected capacity factor with its 90% band from the fitted curve, in percentage points
idea.oneNote: This band covers the fitted curve's uncertainty, not next year's weather.
idea.binsTitle: How the capacity factor is averaged (the maker's curve)
idea.how: Capacity factor = the sum, over wind speeds, of share of the year's hours × power, divided by the 2,000 kW rating. Every curve on this page is averaged the same way.
idea.mix: The wind-speed mix is an illustrative Weibull (k = 2, c = 8 m/s), the same for every curve; output below 3 m/s and above 20 m/s ({above} of hours) counts as zero.
idea.binsCaption: Rounded; the total is summed in 0.1 m/s steps before rounding

explainer.summary: Text version of the explainer: its synthetic turbine at 5, 10 and 25 measured points
explainer.note: From the explainer's own synthetic data: estimates and 95% bands of the curve at each region's centre, in kW. The slider starts at 5 points.
